glossary.title: Glossary
glossary.lead: These are the words that appear in Jelly Cut and on these pages. Type a word into the search.
glossary.empty: No match. Try another word, for example sound or file.

abspielkopf.text: The vertical line on the timeline. It shows which picture you see right now. You can drag it with the mouse.

abtastrate.text: How often per second the sound is measured. 48,000 times per second is common for videos. More measurements sound more exact, but the file gets bigger.

aufkleber.text: A small picture or sign that you put over the video, for example a star or a thumbs up. You can move, turn and enlarge it.

aufloesung.text: How many dots (pixels) a picture has, for example 1920 × 1080. More pixels show more detail, but make the file bigger.

autosave.text: Jelly Cut saves your work automatically in this browser. The display at the top shows whether everything is saved. You can also save the project as a file.

bild.text: A single still picture. A video is a fast row of many pictures. A picture is called a frame.

bildrate.text: How many pictures per second a video has, for example 30 fps (frames per second). More pictures look smoother, but make the file bigger.

bitrate.text: How much data per second is stored in the file, for example 8 megabit per second. In Jelly Cut you choose the quality, and the bitrate follows from it. Higher means better quality and a bigger file.

clip.text: A piece of video, picture or sound that lies on the timeline. You can split, trim and move a clip.

codec.text: The recipe that packs pictures and unpacks them again, for example H.264, VP9 or AV1. Sender and receiver need the same recipe.

container.text: The box that holds pictures, sound and information. The ending such as .mp4 or .webm says which box it is.
container.keys: box file ending mp4 webm mov mkv

credits.text: The names of the creators and the sources of the pictures, music and videos you use. Jelly Cut builds a text from it that you can copy.

einpassen-fuellen.text: Fit shows the whole picture, with bars at the sides. Fill crops the picture so the screen is completely filled.

export.text: Saving the finished video as a file. All clips, texts and filters are calculated and encoded together.

feinschnitt.text: A tool that lets you go picture by picture and cut at exactly one spot. You can also see the keyframes.

filter.text: A colour look, for example black and white, sepia or vintage. With brightness, contrast and saturation you adjust the colours yourself.
filter.keys: colours look black white sepia brightness contrast saturation

format.text: The kind of finished file. MP4 is a video that runs almost everywhere. GIF is a short, silent loop that repeats forever.

keyframe.text: A complete picture in the video. The pictures after it often save only what changes. That is why a video is easiest to cut and play at keyframes.

kodieren.text: Encoding packs pictures into a smaller file. Decoding rebuilds the pictures so you can watch or edit them.

lautstaerke.text: How loud a clip or sound is. In Jelly Cut you set it in percent: 100 % means unchanged.

lizenz.text: The rule that says what you may do with a picture, video or sound. It is on the page where you found the material.

mono-stereo.text: Mono has one sound channel, stereo has two: one for the left and one for the right. Stereo sounds more spacious.

seitenverhaeltnis.text: The ratio of width to height of a picture. Landscape is wide, like a TV. Portrait is tall, like a phone. Square is equally wide and tall.
seitenverhaeltnis.keys: landscape portrait square format width height

spur.text: A row on the timeline, or one part of a file. Video, sound, music, text and overlays each have their own tracks.

standbild.text: A picture that is held and stays still for a while. There is no sound during it.

tempo.text: How fast a clip runs. At double speed the clip runs twice as fast and is half as long.

transparenz.text: How see-through a picture, a text or a sticker is. 100 % is solid, 0 % is invisible. The see-through part of a picture is stored in the alpha channel.

uebergang.text: How one clip changes into the next. For example with a fade, a wipe or a zoom.

ueberblenden.text: A transition: the one picture slowly becomes see-through while the next one appears. A classic.

ueberlagerung.text: Something that lies on top of the video: text, stickers, shapes, drawings or a second picture. It has its own track on the timeline.
ueberlagerung.keys: overlay text sticker shape drawing track

untertitel.text: Text at the bottom of the picture that matches the spoken words. Each subtitle has a start and an end time.

verpixeln.text: An area is split into big squares so that details can no longer be seen. For example for faces or car number plates.

weichzeichnen.text: An area is made blurry. That is good for making people or writing unrecognisable.

wellenform.text: A line that shows how loud the sound is at each moment. High peaks are loud spots.

zeitleiste.text: The bar at the bottom where all clips, texts and sounds lie in order. Time runs from left to right.
